terms.meaning: A check that confirms a value has a known shape, so the program can use it safely.
A value whose type has not been confirmed yet.
A small picture used as a symbol, here a warning triangle.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Icon import
sections.what: Brings in the warning triangle icon used to flag an issue.
sections.why: Likely reason: a visible warning sign for figures that are in dispute.

sections.name: Field
sections.title: Shape of one disputed field
sections.what: Describes a disputed field: its name, the previous value, currency and unit, the reason, and the sources with their check status.
sections.why: Gives the screen a fixed shape to work with.

sections.name: labels
sections.title: Field labels
sections.what: Maps three internal field names, for planned budget, actual cost and delay, to the plain labels shown to the user.
sections.why: So the owner reads readable text instead of internal names.
sections.watch_out: A field name not in this list is rejected by the check in the next section, so it will not be shown.

sections.name: isField
sections.title: Data check
sections.what: Confirms that incoming data has the right shape before the screen uses it: a known field name, a reason, a value that is text or a number, a unit, and a list of sources, each with a link, title and status. Returns true or false.
sections.why: Likely reason: server data is not trusted, so a bad item is skipped instead of crashing the screen.
sections.watch_out: It tests the field name with a plain lookup in the label list, which also matches inherited names such as toString, so such a name would pass the first part of the check.

sections.name: safeSource
sections.title: Checking that a source link is a web address
sections.what: Decides whether a reference link can be shown as a clickable link. Only addresses starting with http or https pass. Anything else, including a broken address, is treated as not safe, so the link is left out.
sections.why: Likely reason: to keep unusual address types from being shown as clickable links. The code does not state this.
sections.watch_out: A reference with a broken or missing address is dropped without any warning, so a reviewer may not know that the reference existed.

sections.name: SourceEvidenceReview
sections.title: Panel listing withheld values
sections.what: Shows a panel explaining that some older figures were withheld because they could not be supported at the stated scope or precision. If the review data is valid, a collapsible list shows each withheld value, its previous number, the reason and any research references with safe links. If the data is not valid, the panel says details are unavailable and points to the audit history.
sections.why: The panel text says withheld values are excluded from calculations rather than treated as zero, and that original values stay in the audit history. The panel is built to make that clear to readers.
sections.watch_out: A withheld value that is not a plain number is shown as NaN in its previous value line.

summary: Checks that a disputed-field record from the server has the right shape before the screen displays it, and gives readable labels for three field names.
purpose: Stops malformed data from breaking the source evidence view, and gives plain names for the disputed fields.
why: Likely reason: data from the server is checked before use. A fuller reason is not stated in the code.
how: 1. Receive a value of unknown type. 2. Reject it if it is empty or not an object. 3. Confirm the field name is one of the three known names. 4. Confirm the reason, value, unit and sources have the right types, and that each source has a link, title and status. 5. Return true only if all checks pass.
inputs: Any value, usually one item from the server's list of disputed fields.
outputs: A true or false answer, and the label list used for display.
risks: Only three field names are accepted, so a new kind of dispute is skipped silently. The name test is loose. The check does not confirm that links work.
debug: If a disputed field does not appear, compare its field name with the three labels, then check the reason, unit and source fields. The rest of the component, which was not shown, displays what passes.
